city.name: Moscow
summary: Moscow was the capital of the Soviet Union and the headquarters of world communism. From the Kremlin the Politburo ran a state of 290 million people and an alliance that reached from East Berlin to Vladivostok. Parades of missiles crossed Red Square past Lenin's tomb twice a year.

Stalin rebuilt the old merchant city with wide avenues and, after the war, seven tiered skyscrapers, the Seven Sisters. Under Khrushchev, from the late 1950s, rings of five-storey concrete blocks went up to rehouse families crowded into communal flats.

In August 1991 hardliners sent tanks into the city to stop the break-up of the Union. Crowds built barricades round the Russian parliament, the White House, and the coup failed in three days. On 25 December the red flag over the Kremlin came down for the last time.
city.note: Shown as it stood in August 1991. Streets and parks are today's OpenStreetMap, which inside the Garden Ring follows the 1991 plan closely; the Third Ring Road, Moscow City and other later works are left out. Streets carry today's names. Moscow gave its streets back their old names between 1990 and 1994, so some still had Soviet names in August 1991 (Bolshaya Nikitskaya was Herzen Street until 1993); only Novy Arbat is shown under its 1991 name, Kalinin Prospekt. The Moskva and the Vodootvodny Canal are today's water outlines. Landmark outlines are from OpenStreetMap. Buildings that are gone (Hotel Rossiya, Hotel Intourist, the Kremlin's Building 14, the Moskva Pool) are drawn by hand from photographs and maps, as are the 1991 barricades and the tanks, so their shapes are approximate. Houses between the streets are generated: pre-revolutionary blocks inside the Garden Ring, Stalin-era blocks on the main avenues, five-storey Khrushchev slabs further out.

properties.name: Vodovzvodnaya Tower
properties.description: The round corner tower on the river. It once held machinery that raised water from the Moskva into the Kremlin.

properties.name: Spasskaya Tower
properties.description: The Kremlin's main gate onto Red Square, built in 1491, with the great clock whose chimes Moscow radio played at midnight. Its ruby star was lit in 1937.

properties.name: Nikolskaya Tower
properties.description: The gate tower at the north end of Red Square. Like the four other gate towers it has carried a glass ruby star, lit from inside, since 1937.

properties.name: Troitskaya Tower
properties.description: The tallest of the Kremlin towers, 80 m, at the end of the bridge from the Kutafya Tower. Visitors to the Palace of Congresses came in through its gate.

properties.name: Borovitskaya Tower
properties.description: The gate used by government cars, at the south-west corner by the Grand Kremlin Palace.

properties.name: Moscow Kremlin
description: The fortress at the heart of Moscow and, from 1918, the seat of Soviet power. Lenin, Stalin and their successors governed from the Senate building inside its walls, and the Politburo met there each Thursday.
Most of the Kremlin's churches were closed after the Revolution and the monasteries inside the walls were demolished in 1929 and 1930. It reopened to the public in 1955.

properties.name: Kremlin wall
properties.description: The brick walls, 2.2 km round and 5 to 19 m high, were built by Italian masters between 1485 and 1495, with twenty towers. The swallowtail merlons are of the Milanese pattern.

properties.name: Cathedral of the Dormition
properties.description: The Kremlin's principal church, built by Aristotele Fioravanti in 1475 to 1479, where the tsars were crowned. Under Soviet rule it was a museum; its first service in seventy years was held in 1990.

properties.name: Cathedral of the Archangel
properties.description: Burial church of the grand princes and tsars of Moscow, from Ivan the Great to Peter the Great's brother Ivan V.

properties.name: Cathedral of the Annunciation
properties.description: The private chapel of the tsars, with nine gilded domes. Its icons are by Theophanes the Greek and Andrei Rublev.

properties.name: Ivan the Great Bell Tower
properties.description: At 81 m the tallest building in Moscow until 1917, built in 1505 to 1508 and raised in 1600 under Boris Godunov. By an old rule nothing in the Kremlin could stand higher.

properties.name: Grand Kremlin Palace
properties.description: Built for Nicholas I in 1838 to 1849. Its great hall was rebuilt in the 1930s for the Supreme Soviet, the Soviet parliament, which met here until 1991.

properties.name: Kremlin Senate
description: Matvey Kazakov's triangular Senate of 1776 to 1787 became the Soviet government's headquarters in 1918. Lenin lived and worked on its third floor; later the General Secretaries had their offices here.
On 25 December 1991 Gorbachev signed his resignation here. That evening the red flag on the dome was lowered.

properties.name: Arsenal
properties.description: Peter the Great's arsenal, finished in 1736. Barracks of the Kremlin guard in Soviet times.

properties.name: Armoury Chamber
properties.description: The treasury museum of the tsars: crowns, Fabergé eggs, carriages and armour.

properties.name: Palace of Congresses
properties.description: Khrushchev's glass and marble hall for the Party congresses, opened in October 1961 for the 22nd Congress. With 6,000 seats it doubled as a theatre for the Bolshoi ballet.

properties.name: Kremlin Building 14
properties.description: Built in 1932 to 1934 on the site of two demolished monasteries, as a school for Red Army commanders. Later the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet met here. It was pulled down in 2016.

properties.name: Red Square
description: The great square under the Kremlin's east wall. On 1 May and 7 November tanks, missiles and marching columns crossed it while the leaders took the salute from the top of Lenin's tomb.
In May 1987 a West German teenager, Mathias Rust, landed a light aircraft next to it, having flown unchallenged from Helsinki.

properties.name: St Basil's Cathedral
properties.description: Ivan the Terrible's cathedral of 1555 to 1561, nine chapels under patterned domes, built to mark the conquest of Kazan. A museum in Soviet times; Stalin is said to have refused to let it be pulled down to widen the square for parades.

properties.name: Lenin's Mausoleum
description: Lenin's embalmed body has lain here since 1924; the granite tomb replaced a wooden one in 1930. From 1953 to 1961 Stalin lay beside him.
Soviet leaders reviewed parades from the tribune on its roof. Behind it, along the wall, are the graves of Stalin, Brezhnev, Andropov and Chernenko.

properties.name: GUM
properties.description: The State Department Store: three glass-roofed arcades of 1893 facing the Kremlin. In Soviet times shoppers queued here for goods hard to find elsewhere; by 1991 many counters stood empty.

properties.name: State Historical Museum
properties.description: The red-brick museum of Russian history (1875 to 1881) closing the north end of Red Square.

properties.name: Bolshoi Theatre
properties.description: Moscow's opera and ballet house, rebuilt in 1856 after a fire, with Apollo's chariot over the portico. Party congresses met here in the early Soviet years.

properties.name: Manezhnaya Square
properties.description: A bare open square in 1991, cleared in the 1930s. Hundreds of thousands gathered here for the democratic rallies of 1990 and 1991, and on 19 August coup troops parked their tanks on it.

properties.name: Manege
properties.description: A riding hall of 1817 used for exhibitions. Here in 1962 Khrushchev shouted down the abstract painters of the Manege affair.

properties.name: Hotel Moskva
properties.description: Stalin's hotel of 1935, with its two mismatched wings, pictured on the Stolichnaya vodka label. Demolished in 2004 and rebuilt as a copy.

properties.name: Hotel Intourist
properties.description: A 22-storey glass and concrete slab of 1970 for foreign tourists at the bottom of Gorky Street. Demolished in 2002. The outline drawn is that of the hotel built on its site.

properties.name: Pashkov House
properties.description: A neoclassical palace of the 1780s on a hill facing the Kremlin, part of the Lenin State Library.

properties.name: Detsky Mir
properties.description: The Soviet Union's biggest toy shop, opened in 1957 across the square from the KGB.

properties.name: Lubyanka (KGB headquarters)
description: Built in 1898 for the Rossiya insurance company and taken over by the Cheka, the Bolshevik secret police, in 1918. Under every later name (OGPU, NKVD, KGB) it was the headquarters of state security, with a prison inside.
Its chairman Vladimir Kryuchkov was a leader of the August 1991 coup.

properties.name: Statue of Felix Dzerzhinsky
description: Yevgeny Vuchetich's bronze of the founder of the Cheka, 'Iron Felix', put up in the middle of Lubyanka Square in 1958.
On the evening of 22 August 1991, after the coup had failed, a crowd tried to pull it down. City officials sent cranes, and it was lifted off its pedestal and driven away.

properties.name: Empty pedestal of Iron Felix
properties.description: The statue was taken down late on 22 August 1991 and dumped in a park by the New Tretyakov Gallery, where it still stands.

properties.name: Solovetsky Stone
properties.description: A boulder from the Solovki prison camp, set up opposite the KGB by the Memorial society in October 1990 in memory of the victims of the Gulag.

properties.name: Hotel Rossiya
properties.description: With some 3,000 rooms the largest hotel in the world when it opened in 1967, built over the old Zaryadye quarter beside Red Square. Delegates to Party congresses stayed here. It was demolished in 2006; Zaryadye Park now fills the site.

properties.name: Moskva Pool
properties.description: A heated open-air pool 130 m across, open all year, built in the foundations of the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, which Stalin blew up in 1931 to make way for a Palace of Soviets that was never built. The cathedral was rebuilt on the site in 1995 to 2000.

properties.name: Moscow State University
properties.wiki: Main building of Moscow State University
properties.description: The largest of the Seven Sisters and the tallest building in Europe until 1990: 240 m to the tip of the star, on the Lenin Hills above the river. Built largely by Gulag prisoners and opened in September 1953, six months after Stalin's death.

properties.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
properties.wiki: Ministry of Foreign Affairs main building
properties.description: The Foreign Ministry tower on Smolensk Square, finished in 1953. Molotov, Gromyko and Shevardnadze ran Soviet diplomacy from here.

properties.name: Hotel Ukraina
properties.description: The last of the Seven Sisters, finished in 1957 at the start of Kutuzovsky Prospekt. Then the tallest hotel in the world.

properties.name: Kudrinskaya Square Building
properties.description: Flats for the Soviet elite (pilots, scientists, artists) on the Garden Ring, finished in 1954, a few hundred metres from the White House.

properties.name: Kotelnicheskaya Embankment Building
properties.description: The first of the Seven Sisters to be finished, in 1952: flats, shops and a cinema where the Yauza meets the Moskva.

properties.name: Red Gates Building
properties.description: Offices of the Ministry of Railways and flats on the Garden Ring, built in 1947 to 1953 over a metro station.

properties.name: Hotel Leningradskaya
properties.description: The smallest of the Seven Sisters, a hotel of 1954 on Komsomolskaya Square, beside the stations for Leningrad, Kazan and Yaroslavl.

properties.name: Kalinin Prospekt tower
properties.description: Kalinin Prospekt (now Novy Arbat) was cut through the old Arbat streets in 1962 to 1968, lined with 24-storey towers of flats on the north side and 26-storey office 'books' on the south.

properties.name: Comecon building
properties.description: Headquarters of Comecon, the Soviet bloc's trade council, finished in 1970: a 31-storey tower opening like a book. Comecon was wound up in June 1991; the Moscow city government took the building.

properties.name: White House (Russian parliament)
description: The House of Soviets of the Russian republic, finished in 1981. In 1991 it was the seat of the Russian parliament and of Boris Yeltsin, elected President of Russia that June.

When the coup began on 19 August, Yeltsin made it the centre of resistance. Tens of thousands of Muscovites built barricades round it and stood guard through two nights, expecting an assault that never came.

properties.name: Yeltsin on the tank
properties.description: Around noon on 19 August Boris Yeltsin climbed onto a T-72 of the Taman Division outside the White House and read an appeal calling the coup illegal and the people to a general strike. The picture went round the world.

properties.name: Tanks that went over to the White House
properties.description: A handful of tank crews under Major Sergei Yevdokimov turned their guns away from the White House and joined its defenders.

properties.name: Barricades round the White House
properties.description: From the afternoon of 19 August the defenders dragged trolleybuses, lorries, concrete blocks, steel bars and paving stones into rings of barricades round the parliament. Drawn approximately.

properties.name: Where three defenders died
properties.description: Shortly after midnight on 21 August armoured vehicles drove into a barricade in the underpass where the Garden Ring passes under Kalinin Prospekt. Dmitry Komar, Vladimir Usov and Ilya Krichevsky were killed. They were made Heroes of the Soviet Union.

properties.name: Coup troops on Manezhnaya Square
properties.description: On the morning of 19 August armoured columns of the Taman and Kantemirov divisions rolled into the centre and parked by the Kremlin walls. Crowds climbed on them to argue with the young conscripts.

properties.name: Old Moscow inside the Garden Ring
